chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala', who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever sells a palm tree that has been pollinated, the fruit belongs to the seller, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise; the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ruled according to that.'

key_terms.لَقِحَ: pollinated (referring to the fruit set on the tree)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the fruit of a palm tree sold after pollination?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of 'fruit follows the tree' in Islamic commercial law, distinguishing between the ownership of the trunk and the produce based on the stage of pollination (*lathiqa*). It underscores the Prophet’s precedent in resolving disputes over asset division, a concept further elaborated in Shia jurisprudence regarding the transfer of risk and benefit in sales contracts. The ruling highlights the importance of explicit stipulation (*shart*) in overriding default ownership structures.
